subject: SOW acceptance criteria, fallback trigger and change order for go-live obligations
messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@medicore.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@medicore.com
Date: 2026-05-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW — small edit request before go-live

Rachel — thanks again for the demo last week. We’re aligned on the implementation milestones but had one request from Procurement and Legal that needs to be reflected in the SOW before we sign:

- Acceptance window: MediCore wants a 14-day acceptance window after cutover with a defined test plan (they supplied a short checklist).
- Fallback trigger: if 3 consecutive production-day regressions > 15% error rate (as measured by our monitoring), Procurement wants an automatic fallback option to previous endpoint and a change order to cover rollback costs.

I attached the checklist and a simple redline that shows where to add language. Can we get a proposal for the change order and confirmation that Redwood can support an automated rollback capability?

Appreciate a quick path here — our board is expecting an ink-by-June target.

— Alex
MediCore Health
Alex Grant | Senior Dir, Procurement
attachments: MediCore_acceptance_checklist.xlsx
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@medicore.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOW — small edit request before go-live

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the checklist. Quick notes:

- We can add a 14-day acceptance period and embed the checklist into Exhibit B.
- "Fallback trigger" semantics are doable but we need to be precise on metrics and the operational steps (who initiates rollback, expected RTO, cost allocation).

I’m looping in Karthik (sales/legal ops) and Laura (billing/procurement liaison) to propose the change order language and the cost treatment for rollbacks. Karthik — can you review the attached redline and draft a short change order that:

  1) Adds the 14-day acceptance language and references MediCore checklist;
  2) Defines the rollback trigger (3 consecutive daily regressions >15% error rate) and required monitoring evidence;
  3) States that if rollback is executed at Redwood’s request or due to platform regression, Redwood will cover rollback runbook hours up to 40 hours; otherwise, rollback costs are billable to MediCore per the standard time-and-materials rate;
  4) Provides a 30-day window post-signature for any implementation fee reconciliation.

Laura — please flag any billing/credit implications. I’ll prepare the redline to the SOW and send a proposed change order for signatures by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: MediCore_SOW_redline_20260527.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Draft change order + fallback language for MediCore

Team — attaching my initial draft. Key points I added:

- Explicit definition of monitoring metric (Daily error rate = failed inference requests / total inference requests, measured over 24h UTC).
- Operational steps: on detection of the trigger, Redwood will notify MediCore within 2 hours, then a 6-hour mitigation window to attempt fixes; if unresolved, rollback may be executed.
- Cost carve: Redwood covers rollback engineering labor up to 40 hours (at no charge); any additional hours billed at 150 USD/hr.

Questions for Legal (Neha): is the rollback “automatic” or should it be discretionary by Redwood ops? If automatic we may need indemnity carveouts. Also, acceptance checklist should be annexed to the SOW rather than inserted inline so it’s auditable.

I’ve included a one-page change order PDF and redline doc.

Attachments: Proposed_ChangeOrder_20260528.pdf; MediCore_SOW_redline_20260527.docx
From: contracts@medicore.com <contracts@medicore.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Grant <alex.grant@medicore.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medicore.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft change order + fallback language for MediCore

Thanks Karthik — procurement/legal reviewed the draft. A few adjustments requested:

- We prefer the rollback to be customer-initiated after Redwood confirms the trigger with evidence. MediCore wants a documented sign-off step to avoid inadvertent rollbacks impacting patients.
- Proposed cap on Redwood-covered rollback hours: 60 hours instead of 40 (they say they need fuller coverage during ramp).
- A clause to guarantee Redwood will not change endpoint behavior without 48h notice except for emergency security fixes.

If Redwood agrees, MediCore is fine with the annex approach for the checklist. Can you provide a redline reflecting those three asks?

— MediCore Contracts (on behalf of Alex Grant)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@medicore.com>, contracts@medicore.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Final redline & sign path — SOW annex + change order

Alex / Contracts team — thanks for the clear feedback. Summary of what we’re proposing based on the thread and internal legal review:

- Acceptance: 14-day acceptance period; checklist in Annex A (auditable).
- Rollback trigger: same metric language but rollback will be Customer-initiated after Redwood provides monitoring evidence and 2-hour confirmation window.
- Redwood rollback coverage: Redwood will cover up to 60 hours of rollback engineering labor at no charge during the initial 30-day ramp post-cutover; additional hours billable per standard SOW rates.
- Endpoint changes: Redwood will provide 48-hour notice for non-emergency behavioral changes; emergency security fixes are excepted.
- Implementation fee reconciliation: 30-day window post-signature for final reconciliation; any credits to be reflected on the first invoice following go-live.

Next steps: I attached the consolidated redline and a one-page change order. If that looks good, please confirm and we’ll route to DocuSign. Aim to have signatures by next Wednesday so we can keep the June go-live.

Thanks — Rachel
